tests.name: FABER Test (Patrickâ€™s Test)
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Affected leg is placed in flexion, abduction, and external rotation (figure-4). Examiner applies gentle downward pressure on knee while stabilizing opposite ASIS.
tests.positiveImplication: Groin pain reproduction or restricted motion indicates hip joint pathology (OA).
tests.negativeImplication: Symmetric, pain-free range of motion without groin pain.

tests.name: FADIR Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes hip to 90Â°, then adducts and internally rotates hip.
tests.positiveImplication: Reproduction of anterior groin pain indicates intra-articular pathology (OA or FAI).
tests.negativeImplication: Smooth, painless internal rotation in flexion.

tests.name: Scour Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes and adducts hip, applies axial compression along femur while sweeping hip in an arc between adduction/internal rotation and abduction/external rotation.
tests.positiveImplication: Groin pain, catching, grinding, or crepitus indicates hip joint degeneration (OA).
tests.negativeImplication: Smooth circumduction arc without pain or crepitus.

tests.name: Log Roll Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls the entire leg into internal and external rotation.
tests.positiveImplication: Groin pain or markedly restricted internal rotation indicates intra-articular hip pathology.

tests.name: Trendelenburg Test
tests.procedure: Patient stands unsupported on affected leg for 30 seconds. Examiner observes pelvic tilt.
tests.positiveImplication: Pelvis on unsupported side drops below horizontal, indicating gluteus medius weakness associated with hip OA.
tests.negativeImplication: Pelvis remains horizontal or slightly elevates on unsupported side.

tests.name: Single-Leg Stance Test
tests.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg unsupported for up to 30 seconds.
tests.positiveImplication: Reproduction of lateral hip pain within 30 seconds indicates gluteal tendinopathy (GTPS).

tests.name: Resisted External Derotation Test
tests.procedure: Patient lies supine with hip and knee flexed to 90Â°. Examiner passively externally rotates hip, then asks patient to return to neutral against resistance.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain reproduced over greater trochanter indicates gluteus medius/minimus tendinopathy.

tests.name: Oberâ€™s Test
tests.procedure: Patient lies on unaffected side. Examiner extends and abducts affected hip, then allows leg to drop into adduction.
tests.positiveImplication: Leg remains abducted and fails to adduct past table, indicating ITB tightness contributing to GTPS.
tests.negativeImplication: Smooth drop into adduction below table horizontal.

tests.name: Trendelenburg Test
tests.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg while examiner observes contralateral pelvic level.
tests.positiveImplication: Pelvic drop on opposite side indicates gluteal abductor dysfunction associated with GTPS.

tests.name: Greater Trochanter Palpation Test
tests.procedure: Examiner applies firm direct palpation over lateral greater trochanter and gluteal tendon insertions.
tests.positiveImplication: Exquisite point tenderness over trochanteric facet indicates GTPS.
tests.negativeImplication: Absence of tenderness over greater trochanter.

tests.name: FADIR Test (Flexion, Adduction, Internal Rotation)
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes hip to 90Â°, then adducts and internally rotates the hip.
tests.positiveImplication: Reproduction of sharp groin pain indicates femoroacetabular impingement.

tests.name: FABER Test (Patrickâ€™s Test)
tests.procedure: Patient is supine with foot on opposite knee (figure-4). Examiner applies downward pressure on ipsilateral knee.
tests.positiveImplication: Anterior groin pain or asymmetric restriction suggests hip joint pathology or FAI.
tests.negativeImplication: Knee reaches table parallel without anterior groin pain.

tests.name: Scour Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes and adducts hip, then applies axial compression while sweeping in an arc.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain, clicking, or mechanical catching indicates labral pathology or FAI.

tests.name: Internal Rotation Overpressure Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine with hip flexed to 90Â°. Examiner applies internal rotation with terminal overpressure.
tests.positiveImplication: Groin pain or marked end-range restriction suggests cam or pincer FAI morphology.
tests.negativeImplication: Normal symmetric internal rotation range without pain.

tests.name: FADIR Test (Labral Impingement)
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner passively flexes, adducts, and internally rotates hip.
tests.positiveImplication: Sharp anterior groin pain or painful click indicates acetabular labral tear.

tests.name: Scour Test (Axial Load)
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner applies axial load through femur while moving hip in circular compression arcs.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain, clicking, popping, or catching sensation confirms labral tear.
tests.negativeImplication: No clicking, popping, or pain under axial load.

tests.name: Log Roll Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls leg into full internal and external rotation.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain or increased external rotation laxity indicates iliofemoral ligament or labral tear.

tests.name: Modified Thomas Test
tests.procedure: Patient lies supine at edge of table, pulling one knee to chest while affected leg hangs extended.
tests.positiveImplication: Groin pain, mechanical clicking, or restriction in the hanging leg indicates labral irritation.
tests.negativeImplication: Hanging leg hangs freely without joint pain or clicking.

tests.name: Log Roll Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls the leg internally and externally.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain in neutral rotation during gentle roll indicates early intra-articular pathology (AVN suspicion).

tests.name: FADIR Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes, adducts, and internally rotates hip.
tests.positiveImplication: Groin pain reproduction suggests intra-articular compromise (evaluated with AVN risk factors).

tests.name: FABER Test
tests.procedure: Patient is supine in figure-4 position. Examiner applies downward pressure on knee.
tests.positiveImplication: Groin pain or severe stiffness indicates femoral head pathology.

tests.name: MRI of Bilateral Hips (Gold Standard)
tests.procedure: T1/T2-weighted MRI of pelvis and both femoral heads.
tests.positiveImplication: Serpiginous low-signal band on T1, 'double-line sign' on T2, or subchondral collapse confirms AVN.
tests.negativeImplication: Normal bone marrow signal and spherical femoral head.

tests.name: Dynamic Hip Movement Test
tests.procedure: Patient actively flexes, abducts, and externally rotates hip, then returns to extension and adduction while examiner palpates.
tests.positiveImplication: Palpable or audible snap over greater trochanter or groin confirms snapping hip.

tests.name: Oberâ€™s Test (External Snapping)
tests.procedure: Patient lies on side. Examiner extends and abducts affected hip, then allows leg to drop toward table.
tests.positiveImplication: Leg remains elevated (ITB tightness) or snapping occurs across trochanter as hip flexes/extends.
tests.negativeImplication: Normal drop into adduction without snap.

tests.name: Thomas Test (Internal Snapping)
tests.procedure: Patient lies supine holding opposite knee to chest while affected hip is extended from flexion.
tests.positiveImplication: Audible or palpable snap in anterior groin as iliopsoas tendon glides over iliopectineal eminence.
